entries.title: Show the current folder
entries.description: Prints the full path of the folder you are currently in.

entries.title: Go to a folder
entries.description: Changes the current folder. Use .. for the parent folder, ~ for your home folder, or a full path like C:\Projects.

entries.title: Go to your Desktop folder
entries.description: Moves to your Desktop folder, even when OneDrive has moved it somewhere else.

entries.title: Go to a folder and remember where you were
entries.description: Saves the current folder on a stack, then moves to another one. Run Pop-Location to jump back.

entries.title: Go back to the previous folder
entries.description: Returns to the folder saved by the last Push-Location. Windows PowerShell has no cd -, so this is the equivalent.

entries.title: List files and folders
entries.description: Shows the files and folders in the current folder with sizes and modified dates.

entries.title: List files including hidden ones
entries.description: Also shows hidden and system items, such as .git folders and dotfiles that a normal listing skips.

entries.title: List only folders
entries.description: Shows only the subfolders of the current folder, not the files.

entries.title: List files sorted by size
entries.description: Lists files in the current folder from largest to smallest. Length is the size in bytes.

entries.title: List files sorted by date, newest first
entries.description: Lists items with the most recently modified at the top.

entries.title: List everything in all subfolders
entries.description: Lists every file and folder below the current folder. Can produce a lot of output in big folders.

entries.title: Show a folder tree
entries.description: Draws the folder structure of the current folder as a tree, including files. Leave off /F to show folders only.

entries.title: Open the current folder in File Explorer
entries.description: Opens File Explorer showing the folder you are in. Same as typing ii . or explorer . in PowerShell.

entries.title: Open a file with its default app
entries.description: Opens a file the same way double-clicking it would, for example a PDF in your PDF viewer.

entries.title: Open the current folder in VS Code
entries.description: Opens the current folder as a project in Visual Studio Code.

entries.title: Get the full path of a file or folder
entries.description: Turns a relative path like ..\notes.txt into a full path. Errors if the path does not exist.

entries.title: Create a folder
entries.description: Creates a folder, including any missing parent folders. -Force means no error if it already exists.

entries.title: Create an empty file
entries.description: Creates a new empty file. It fails if the file already exists, so nothing gets overwritten.

params.name: file
params.description: Name or path of the new file

entries.title: Write text to a file (overwrite)
entries.description: Replaces the whole file with the text you give, creating it if needed. Use Add-Content to append instead.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to put in the file

entries.title: Append a line of text to a file
entries.description: Adds text as a new line at the end of a file, creating the file if needed.

entries.title: Show the contents of a file
entries.description: Prints a text file to the terminal.

entries.title: Show the first lines of a file
entries.description: Prints only the first few lines, without reading the rest of a big file.

entries.title: Show the last lines of a file
entries.description: Prints only the last few lines, which is where log files keep their newest entries.

entries.title: Follow a log file as it grows (tail -f)
entries.description: Shows the last 20 lines, then keeps printing new lines as they are written. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

entries.title: Copy a file
entries.description: Copies a file to a new location or name. Overwrites the destination without asking if it already exists.

params.name: destination
params.description: New path or folder for the copy

entries.title: Copy a folder and its contents
entries.description: Copies a folder and everything in it. If the destination folder already exists, the copy goes inside it.

entries.title: Copy a large folder reliably with robocopy
entries.description: Copies a folder tree with retries and a summary, skipping files that are already up to date. Good for big or network copies.

entries.title: Move a file or folder
entries.description: Moves a file or folder to another location. Fails if something with the same name is already there.

params.name: destination
params.description: Folder or new path to move it to

entries.title: Rename a file or folder
entries.description: Renames a file or folder in place. Give only the new name, not a full path.

params.name: new-name
params.description: New name, without a folder path

entries.title: Replace text in many file names
entries.description: Renames files in the current folder by swapping text in their names. Uses regex, so escape characters like . and ( with a backslash.

params.name: find
params.description: Text or regex to find in names

params.name: replace
params.description: Text to put in its place

entries.title: Delete a file permanently
entries.description: Deletes a file. It does not go to the Recycle Bin, so it cannot be restored.

entries.title: Delete a folder and everything in it
entries.description: Permanently deletes the folder and all of its contents, including hidden files, with no Recycle Bin and no prompt. Check the path first.

entries.title: Delete all files matching a pattern
entries.description: Permanently deletes every matching file in a folder and its subfolders. Run it without the final | Remove-Item first to preview.

entries.title: Preview what a delete would remove
entries.description: Lists what would be deleted without deleting anything. Most commands that change things accept -WhatIf.

params.name: path
params.description: File, folder or wildcard you plan to delete

entries.title: Move a file to the Recycle Bin
entries.description: Deletes a file the way Explorer does, so it lands in the Recycle Bin and can be restored later.

params.name: file
params.description: File to send to the Recycle Bin

entries.title: Show details about a file
entries.description: Shows everything PowerShell knows about a file: full path, size in bytes, created and modified dates and attributes.

entries.title: Get the total size of a folder
entries.description: Adds up every file in a folder and its subfolders and prints the total in MB. Can take a while on big folders.

entries.title: Find files larger than a size
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Path <folder> -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB * <megabytes> } | Sort-Object -Property Length -Descending | Select-Object -Property FullName, @{Name='SizeMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 1)}}
entries.description: Lists every file over the given size in MB, biggest first. Handy for freeing up disk space.
entries.example: Get-ChildItem -Path $HOME -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB * 500 } | Sort-Object -Property Length -Descending | Select-Object -Property FullName, @{Name='SizeMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 1)}}

entries.title: List the 20 largest files in a folder tree
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Path <folder> -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object -Property Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 20 -Property FullName, @{Name='SizeMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 1)}}
entries.description: Shows the 20 biggest files anywhere under a folder, with sizes in MB.
entries.example: Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object -Property Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 20 -Property FullName, @{Name='SizeMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 1)}}

entries.title: Find files changed in the last few days
entries.description: Lists files modified within the given number of days, newest first.

params.name: days
params.description: How many days back to look

entries.title: Check whether a file or folder exists
entries.description: Prints True if something exists at that path, False if not.

entries.title: Compare two text files
entries.description: Shows lines that differ. <= marks lines only in the first file, => marks lines only in the second.

entries.title: Get a file's SHA-256 checksum
entries.description: Computes a checksum to check a download matches the one the vendor publishes. Use -Algorithm MD5 or SHA1 if that is what they list.

entries.title: Check a download against a published checksum
entries.description: Prints True if the file's SHA-256 matches the checksum you paste. Upper or lower case does not matter.

params.name: expected-hash
params.description: SHA-256 value published by the vendor

entries.title: Create a symbolic link
entries.description: Makes a link that programs treat as the real file or folder. Needs an admin window or Windows Developer Mode turned on.

params.name: target
params.description: Existing file or folder it points to

entries.title: Link a folder to another folder (junction)
entries.description: Makes a folder that points at another folder on this PC. Unlike symlinks, junctions do not need admin rights.

params.name: link
params.description: Path of the new linked folder

entries.title: Show a file's attributes (hidden, read-only)
entries.description: Shows flags such as Hidden, ReadOnly, System and Archive for a file or folder.

entries.title: Hide a file or folder
entries.description: Marks a file or folder as hidden so Explorer and normal listings skip it. Undo with attrib -h.

entries.title: Make a file read-only
entries.description: Protects a file from being changed. Run it again with $false to make it writable.

entries.title: Open a file in Notepad
entries.description: Opens the file in Notepad for editing. If the file does not exist, Notepad offers to create it.

entries.title: Find and replace text in a file
entries.description: Replaces every match in a file and saves it as UTF-8. The search is a regex, so escape characters like . or ( with a backslash.

entries.title: Convert Windows line endings to Unix (LF)
entries.description: Changes CRLF line endings to LF in place, keeping the text as UTF-8. Fixes shell scripts that fail with \r errors on Linux.

entries.title: Find files by name in all subfolders
entries.description: Searches a folder and everything below it for matching names. Use * as a wildcard, e.g. *invoice*.

entries.title: Find all files with an extension
entries.description: Lists every file of one type under a folder, e.g. all .pdf or .js files.

entries.title: Find a folder by name
entries.description: Searches for folders, not files, whose name matches. Wildcards like *test* work.

entries.title: Find empty folders
entries.description: Lists folders that contain nothing at all, not even hidden files.

entries.title: Find duplicate files
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Path <folder> -Recurse -File | Get-FileHash | Group-Object -Property Hash | Where-Object { $_.Count -gt 1 } | ForEach-Object { $_.Group.Path; '' }
entries.description: Hashes every file and prints groups of identical files, separated by blank lines. Slow on big folders because every file is read.
entries.example: Get-ChildItem -Path $HOME\Pictures -Recurse -File | Get-FileHash | Group-Object -Property Hash | Where-Object { $_.Count -gt 1 } | ForEach-Object { $_.Group.Path; '' }

entries.title: Search for text in a file
entries.description: Prints each matching line with its line number. Not case-sensitive by default, and the pattern is a regex.

params.name: text
params.description: Text or regex to look for

entries.title: Search for text in all files under a folder
entries.description: Searches every file under a folder and prints the file, line number and matching line.

params.name: text
params.description: Text or regex to look for

entries.title: Search text only in files of one type
entries.description: Like grep -r but limited to matching files, e.g. only *.py, which is faster and skips binary files.

params.name: text
params.description: Text or regex to look for

entries.title: List files that contain some text
entries.description: Prints only the names of files that contain a match, one per file.

params.name: text
params.description: Text or regex to look for

entries.title: Search for exact text (no regex)
entries.description: Searches for the text exactly as typed, so characters like . ( $ and * need no escaping.

entries.title: Show lines that do not match
entries.description: Prints every line that does NOT contain the pattern, which is useful for filtering noise out of logs.

params.name: text
params.description: Text or regex to leave out

entries.title: Search text and show surrounding lines
entries.description: Shows each match with a few lines before and after it. The matching line is marked with >.

params.name: text
params.description: Text or regex to look for

params.name: lines
params.description: Lines of context before and after

entries.title: Extract only the matching text (grep -o)
entries.description: Prints just the parts that match a regex, such as every email address or URL in a file.

entries.title: Find and replace text across many files
entries.description: Rewrites every matching file under a folder, saving them as UTF-8. Uses regex. Commit or back up first, as there is no undo.

entries.title: Extract a .zip archive
entries.description: Unpacks every file in a .zip archive into a folder, creating the folder if needed.

entries.title: Extract a .zip and overwrite existing files
entries.description: Unpacks a .zip into a folder, replacing any files that already exist there with the versions from the zip.

entries.title: Zip a folder
entries.description: Creates a .zip containing the folder. Fails if the zip already exists (add -Force to overwrite). Windows PowerShell handles up to 2 GB.

entries.title: Zip the contents of a folder (not the folder itself)
entries.description: Zips everything inside a folder so the files sit at the top level of the zip, which many upload sites expect.

entries.title: Zip files that match a pattern
entries.description: Zips every file matching a wildcard, such as all .log files in a folder.

entries.title: List what is inside an archive
entries.description: Lists the files inside a .zip, .tar, .tgz or .tar.gz without extracting anything. Uses the tar built into Windows 10 and later.

entries.title: Create a .tar.gz (tgz) archive
entries.description: Packs a folder into a gzip-compressed tarball, the usual format for Linux servers.

entries.title: Extract a .tar.gz, .tgz or .tar file
entries.description: Unpacks a tarball into the current folder. The tar built into Windows can also extract .zip files.

entries.title: Extract a tarball into a specific folder
entries.description: Unpacks a .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar or .zip into a folder. The folder must already exist.

entries.title: Extract .7z, .rar and other archives with 7-Zip
entries.description: Unpacks almost any archive format, keeping its folder structure. Needs 7-Zip installed with 7z on your PATH.

entries.title: List running processes
entries.description: Shows every running program with its process ID, memory and CPU time.

entries.title: Find a running process by name
entries.description: Shows processes with that name. Leave off .exe, and use wildcards like *chrome* if unsure. Errors if none are running.

entries.title: Show processes with their full command line
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Process | Select-Object -Property ProcessId, ParentProcessId, Name, CommandLine
entries.description: Lists every process with its parent ID and the exact command line it was started with.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Process | Select-Object -Property ProcessId, ParentProcessId, Name, CommandLine

entries.title: Show the processes using the most CPU
entries.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object -Property CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 -Property Name, Id, CPU, @{Name='MemoryMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB)}}
entries.description: Lists the 10 processes that have used the most processor time. CPU is total seconds since each one started, not a live percentage.
entries.example: Get-Process | Sort-Object -Property CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 -Property Name, Id, CPU, @{Name='MemoryMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB)}}

entries.title: Show the processes using the most memory
entries.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object -Property WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 -Property Name, Id, @{Name='MemoryMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB)}}
entries.description: Lists the 10 processes using the most RAM right now, in MB.
entries.example: Get-Process | Sort-Object -Property WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 -Property Name, Id, @{Name='MemoryMB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB)}}

entries.title: Watch top processes live (like top)
entries.command: while ($true) { Clear-Host; Get-Process | Sort-Object -Property CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 15 -Property Name, Id, CPU, WorkingSet64 | Format-Table -AutoSize; Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }
entries.description: Refreshes a table of the busiest processes every 2 seconds. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
entries.example: while ($true) { Clear-Host; Get-Process | Sort-Object -Property CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 15 -Property Name, Id, CPU, WorkingSet64 | Format-Table -AutoSize; Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }

entries.title: Find programs that are not responding
entries.description: Lists windowed programs that Windows considers frozen.

entries.title: Kill a process by name
entries.description: Closes every process with that name right away. Unsaved work in those programs is lost. Leave off .exe.

entries.title: Kill a process by its ID
entries.description: Force-closes one process using its ID (PID), which you can find with Get-Process. Unsaved work is lost.

entries.title: Kill a program and all its child processes
entries.description: Force-closes a program plus everything it started, which helps with dev servers that leave child processes behind. Include .exe.

entries.title: Kill whatever is using a port
entries.command: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen | Select-Object -ExpandProperty OwningProcess -Unique | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_ -Force }
entries.description: Finds the program listening on a TCP port and force-closes it. Fixes "port already in use" errors. Some system processes need an admin window.
entries.example: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3000 -State Listen | Select-Object -ExpandProperty OwningProcess -Unique | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_ -Force }

entries.title: Start a program
entries.description: Launches a program or opens a file or URL in a new window, without tying up the terminal.

entries.title: Start a program as administrator
entries.description: Launches a program with admin rights. Windows shows a UAC prompt to confirm.

entries.title: Run a command in the background
entries.description: Runs a command as a background job so you can keep working. Jobs start in your Documents folder, so use full paths. Check on it with Get-Job.

entries.title: List background jobs
entries.description: Shows background jobs in this session with their ID and state (Running, Completed, Failed).

entries.title: Get the output of a background job
entries.description: Prints what a background job has produced so far. -Keep leaves the output in place so you can read it again.

entries.title: Show full network configuration
entries.description: Lists every network adapter with its IP address, MAC address, gateway and DNS servers.

entries.title: Show my local IP address
entries.description: Lists the IPv4 address of each network adapter. Your LAN address usually starts with 192.168 or 10.

entries.title: Show my public IP address
entries.description: Asks a free web service which address your traffic appears to come from on the internet.

entries.title: Ping a host
entries.description: Sends 4 pings and shows the response time of each. Some servers block ping, so no reply does not always mean down.

entries.title: Trace the route to a host
entries.description: Shows each router hop between you and a host and how long each takes. Useful to see where a connection slows down.

entries.title: Look up the IP address of a domain
entries.description: Asks DNS which IP addresses a domain name points to.

entries.title: Look up a specific DNS record type (MX, TXT...)
entries.description: Fetches one kind of DNS record, e.g. MX for mail servers or TXT for SPF and verification records.

params.name: record-type
params.description: Record type such as A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME or NS

entries.title: Check whether a port is open on a host
entries.description: Tries to connect to a TCP port. TcpTestSucceeded True means something is listening and no firewall blocked it.

entries.title: Check whether the internet is working
entries.description: Runs a quick connectivity test to a Microsoft server and reports whether ping and DNS work.

entries.title: Find which program is using a port
entries.command: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen | Select-Object -ExpandProperty OwningProcess -Unique | ForEach-Object { Get-Process -Id $_ }
entries.description: Shows the program listening on a TCP port. Errors if nothing is listening there.
entries.example: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8080 -State Listen | Select-Object -ExpandProperty OwningProcess -Unique | ForEach-Object { Get-Process -Id $_ }

entries.title: List listening ports and their programs
entries.command: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object -Property LocalPort | Select-Object -Property LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess, @{Name='Process'; Expression={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess).ProcessName}}
entries.description: Lists every TCP port your PC is listening on with the program that owns it.
entries.example: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object -Property LocalPort | Select-Object -Property LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess, @{Name='Process'; Expression={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess).ProcessName}}

entries.title: Show all connections with process IDs (netstat)
entries.description: Classic list of every TCP and UDP connection and listening port, with the owning process ID in the last column.

entries.title: Flush the DNS cache
entries.description: Clears remembered DNS lookups so changed websites or hosts-file edits take effect right away.

entries.title: Show which DNS servers I use
entries.description: Lists the DNS servers configured for each network adapter.

entries.title: Download a file from a URL
entries.description: Saves a file from the web. Turning off the progress bar makes downloads much faster in Windows PowerShell.

entries.title: Download a file with curl
entries.description: Uses the curl built into Windows to download a file, following redirects. Type curl.exe, since curl alone is an alias in Windows PowerShell.

entries.title: Show current Wi-Fi connection details
entries.description: Shows the Wi-Fi network you are on, signal strength, speed, channel and band.

entries.title: Show a saved Wi-Fi password
entries.command: netsh wlan show profile name=<network> key=clear
entries.description: Shows the settings of a saved Wi-Fi network. The password is on the Key Content line; run in an admin window if it is missing.

params.name: network
params.description: Name (SSID) of the saved Wi-Fi network

entries.example: netsh wlan show profile name=HomeWiFi key=clear

entries.title: Show the hosts file
entries.description: Prints the Windows hosts file, which maps names to IPs before DNS is asked. It lives in C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc.

entries.title: Edit the hosts file as administrator
entries.description: Opens the hosts file in Notepad with admin rights so you can save changes. Mistakes can break websites, so keep a backup.

entries.title: List network adapters
entries.description: Shows each network adapter with its status (Up or Disconnected), MAC address and link speed.

entries.title: Show my default gateway (router IP)
entries.description: Shows the router address your traffic goes through, which is usually the address of your router's admin page.

entries.title: List devices seen on the local network
entries.description: Shows IP and MAC addresses of devices your PC has talked to recently on the local network.

entries.title: Release and renew the IP address
entries.description: Drops the current IP and asks the router for a new one. Your connection drops for a few seconds.

entries.title: Call a web API and show the JSON
entries.description: Sends a GET request and turns the JSON response into objects you can read or filter.

entries.title: Send JSON to an API (POST)
entries.description: Sends a POST request with a JSON body and shows the response.

entries.title: Show the HTTP headers of a URL
entries.description: Fetches only the response headers, e.g. to check content type, caching or server software.

entries.title: Check the HTTP status code of a URL
entries.description: Prints only the status code, such as 200 or 404, which is good for checking a site is up.

entries.title: Open a website in the default browser
entries.description: Opens a link in your default web browser.

entries.title: Fix "Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel"
entries.description: Turns on TLS 1.2 for web requests in this window. Old Windows PowerShell setups sometimes need this to reach modern sites.

entries.title: Show the Windows version
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object -Property Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
entries.description: Shows the Windows edition, version, build number and whether it is 64-bit.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object -Property Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture

entries.title: Show how long the PC has been running
entries.description: Shows the time since the last restart in days, hours and minutes. Fast Startup can make shut down count as not restarting.

entries.title: Show a full system summary
entries.description: Lists Windows version, hardware, BIOS, memory, time zone and much more. Takes a few seconds.

entries.title: Show CPU model and core count
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Processor | Select-Object -Property Name, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors, MaxClockSpeed
entries.description: Shows the processor model, physical cores, threads and maximum speed in MHz.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Processor | Select-Object -Property Name, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors, MaxClockSpeed

entries.title: Show current CPU usage percentage
entries.description: Shows how busy each processor is right now as a percentage.

entries.title: Show free and total memory
entries.description: Shows how much RAM is free right now compared with the total.

entries.title: Show graphics card and screen resolution
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_VideoController | Select-Object -Property Name, DriverVersion, CurrentHorizontalResolution, CurrentVerticalResolution
entries.description: Shows each graphics adapter, its driver version and the current resolution.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_VideoController | Select-Object -Property Name, DriverVersion, CurrentHorizontalResolution, CurrentVerticalResolution

entries.title: Create and open a battery health report
entries.description: Saves battery-report.html in the current folder and opens it. Compare Design Capacity with Full Charge Capacity to see wear.

entries.title: Show battery charge level
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Battery | Select-Object -Property Name, EstimatedChargeRemaining, EstimatedRunTime
entries.description: Shows the battery percentage and estimated minutes left. Shows nothing on a desktop without a battery.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Battery | Select-Object -Property Name, EstimatedChargeRemaining, EstimatedRunTime

entries.title: List installed programs
entries.command: Get-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*, HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*, HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } | Select-Object -Property DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher | Sort-Object -Property DisplayName
entries.description: Lists programs from Add or Remove Programs with their version and publisher. Store apps are not included.
entries.example: Get-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*, HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*, HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } | Select-Object -Property DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher | Sort-Object -Property DisplayName

entries.title: Show recent system errors from the event log
entries.description: Lists the 20 latest errors from the Windows System log, the same data Event Viewer shows.

entries.title: Show recent app crashes and errors
entries.description: Lists the 20 latest errors from the Application log, which records program crashes.

entries.title: Find unexpected shutdowns and crashes
entries.description: Lists times Windows stopped without shutting down cleanly, such as power loss, freezes or blue screens.

entries.title: List installed Windows updates
entries.description: Lists installed Windows updates (KB numbers), newest first.

entries.title: List programs that start with Windows
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_StartupCommand | Select-Object -Property Name, Command, Location, User
entries.description: Shows apps set to launch when you sign in. Turn them off in Task Manager under Startup apps.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_StartupCommand | Select-Object -Property Name, Command, Location, User

entries.title: Find devices with driver problems
entries.description: Lists connected hardware that Windows reports as having an error, such as a missing driver.

entries.title: Show the computer name
entries.description: Prints this PC's network name.

entries.title: Show the current user
entries.description: Prints the signed-in account as COMPUTER\username or DOMAIN\username.

entries.title: Show the current date and time
entries.description: Prints today's date and the current time.

entries.title: Restart the computer
entries.description: Restarts Windows right away. Unsaved work in open programs may be lost.

entries.title: Shut down the computer
entries.description: Shuts down Windows right away. Unsaved work in open programs may be lost.

entries.title: Shut down after a delay
entries.description: Schedules a shutdown after the given number of seconds, e.g. 3600 for one hour. Cancel it with shutdown /a.

entries.title: Lock the screen
entries.description: Locks Windows straight away, just like pressing Win+L.

entries.title: Scan and repair Windows system files
entries.description: Checks protected Windows files and replaces corrupted ones. Needs an admin window and takes 10-20 minutes.

entries.title: Open Task Manager
entries.description: Opens Task Manager to see running apps, performance graphs and startup apps.

entries.title: Show free space on all drives (df)
entries.description: Lists each drive letter with used and free space in GB.

entries.title: Show drive size, free space and percent free
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter 'DriveType=3' | Select-Object -Property DeviceID, @{Name='SizeGB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 1)}}, @{Name='FreeGB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1GB, 1)}}, @{Name='FreePct'; Expression={[math]::Round(100 * $_.FreeSpace / $_.Size)}}
entries.description: Lists local drives with total size, free space and percentage free.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter 'DriveType=3' | Select-Object -Property DeviceID, @{Name='SizeGB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 1)}}, @{Name='FreeGB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1GB, 1)}}, @{Name='FreePct'; Expression={[math]::Round(100 * $_.FreeSpace / $_.Size)}}

entries.title: List drives and volumes
entries.description: Lists each volume with its drive letter, label, file system, health and size.

entries.title: List physical disks and their health
entries.command: Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object -Property FriendlyName, MediaType, BusType, HealthStatus, @{Name='SizeGB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB)}}
entries.description: Shows each physical disk, whether it is an SSD or HDD, how it is connected and its health status.
entries.example: Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object -Property FriendlyName, MediaType, BusType, HealthStatus, @{Name='SizeGB'; Expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB)}}

entries.title: Show what is using disk space in a folder
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Path <folder> -Directory -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ Folder = $_.Name; SizeGB = [math]::Round((Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum / 1GB, 2) } } | Sort-Object -Property SizeGB -Descending
entries.description: Totals the size of each subfolder, biggest first, so you can see where your space went. Slow on whole drives.
keywords: what is using my disk space
entries.example: Get-ChildItem -Path $HOME -Directory -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ Folder = $_.Name; SizeGB = [math]::Round((Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum / 1GB, 2) } } | Sort-Object -Property SizeGB -Descending

entries.title: Empty the Recycle Bin
entries.description: Permanently deletes everything in the Recycle Bin on all drives to free up space.

entries.title: Delete temporary files
entries.description: Deletes files in your user temp folder to free space. Files that programs are using are skipped.

entries.title: Check a drive for errors
entries.description: Scans a drive's file system for errors without fixing them. Needs an admin window. Add /f to fix (C: needs a restart).

params.name: drive
params.description: Drive letter with colon, e.g. D:

entries.title: List mapped network drives
entries.description: Shows network shares mapped to drive letters and whether they are connected.

entries.title: List all environment variables
entries.description: Shows every environment variable in this session with its value.

entries.title: Show the value of an environment variable
entries.description: Prints the value of one variable, e.g. JAVA_HOME. Same as typing $env:JAVA_HOME. Prints nothing if it is not set.

entries.title: Set an environment variable for this session
entries.description: Sets a variable for this PowerShell window and programs started from it. It disappears when you close the window.

entries.title: Set an environment variable permanently
entries.description: Saves a variable for your user account. Only newly opened terminals see it, so restart your terminal afterwards.

entries.title: Show PATH entries one per line
entries.description: Lists every folder Windows searches for commands, in the order it searches them.

entries.title: Add a folder to PATH for this session
entries.description: Lets you run programs from that folder in this window only. Closing the window undoes it.

entries.title: Add a folder to PATH permanently
entries.description: Appends a folder to your user PATH for good. Open a new terminal to use it. Check it is not already there to avoid duplicates.

entries.title: Reload PATH without reopening the terminal
entries.description: Rebuilds PATH from the saved system and user values so newly installed tools work in this window.

entries.title: Show where AppData, Temp and other folders are
entries.description: Prints the real paths of common special folders such as %APPDATA% and %TEMP%.

entries.title: Load variables from a .env file
entries.description: Sets each NAME=value line as an environment variable for this window, skipping comments. Quotes around values are kept as-is.

entries.title: List all services
entries.description: Shows every Windows service with its status (Running or Stopped).

entries.title: Find a service and its status
entries.description: Finds services by their friendly name. Wildcards work, e.g. *SQL*.

entries.title: Show a service's startup type and program path
entries.command: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq <name> } | Select-Object -Property Name, State, StartMode, PathName, StartName
entries.description: Shows whether a service starts automatically, which account it runs as and its executable.
entries.example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'Spooler' } | Select-Object -Property Name, State, StartMode, PathName, StartName

entries.title: Start a service
entries.description: Starts a Windows service. Usually needs an admin window.

entries.title: Stop a service
entries.description: Stops a Windows service and anything that depends on it may stop working. Usually needs an admin window.

entries.title: Restart a service
entries.description: Stops and starts a service again, a common fix for stuck printers, audio or networking. Usually needs an admin window.

entries.title: Change how a service starts
entries.description: Sets a service to Automatic, Manual or Disabled. Disabling the wrong service can break Windows features. Needs an admin window.

entries.title: List scheduled tasks
entries.command: Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.State -ne 'Disabled' } | Select-Object -Property TaskPath, TaskName, State
entries.description: Lists enabled tasks in Task Scheduler, including ones Windows and other apps created.
entries.example: Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.State -ne 'Disabled' } | Select-Object -Property TaskPath, TaskName, State

entries.title: Show when a scheduled task last and next runs
entries.description: Shows the last run time, last result (0 means success) and next run time of a task.

entries.title: Run a program every day at a set time
entries.description: Creates a Task Scheduler task that runs daily while you are signed in. Times like 9am or 21:30 work.

entries.title: Delete a scheduled task
entries.description: Permanently removes a task from Task Scheduler, with no confirmation prompt.

entries.title: Wait for a number of seconds
entries.description: Pauses for the given time. Handy between commands in a script.

entries.title: Re-run a command every few seconds (watch)
entries.description: Clears the screen and runs the command again on a loop. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

entries.title: Show the script execution policy
entries.description: Shows which script policy applies at each level. Restricted blocks all .ps1 scripts, the default on many PCs.

entries.title: Allow running your own PowerShell scripts
entries.description: Lets your own .ps1 scripts (like a venv's Activate.ps1) run. Downloaded scripts still need signing or unblocking. Affects your account only.

entries.title: Run one script without changing the policy
entries.description: Runs a single .ps1 file in a new PowerShell process that ignores the execution policy. Only do this for scripts you trust.

entries.title: Unblock a downloaded file
entries.description: Removes the downloaded-from-the-internet mark, so scripts can run and Office stops showing Protected View. Only for files you trust.

entries.title: Check if this window is running as admin
entries.description: Prints True if this PowerShell window has administrator rights.

entries.title: Show who can access a file or folder
entries.description: Shows the owner and the permission entries (ACL) on a file or folder.
entries.example: Get-Acl -Path C:\Projects | Format-List -Property Path, Owner, AccessToString

entries.title: Take ownership of a file or folder
entries.description: Makes you the owner of a file or folder and everything inside, to fix access denied errors. Needs an admin window.

entries.title: Check Windows Defender antivirus status
entries.command: Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object -Property AntivirusEnabled, RealTimeProtectionEnabled, AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated, QuickScanEndTime
entries.description: Shows whether antivirus and real-time protection are on and when virus definitions were last updated.
entries.example: Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object -Property AntivirusEnabled, RealTimeProtectionEnabled, AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated, QuickScanEndTime

entries.title: Scan a file or folder for viruses
entries.description: Runs Windows Defender on one file or folder. Threats it finds are quarantined.

entries.title: Check whether the firewall is on
entries.command: Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object -Property Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction
entries.description: Shows the Domain, Private and Public firewall profiles and whether each is enabled.
entries.example: Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object -Property Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction

entries.title: List enabled inbound firewall rules
entries.command: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Enabled True | Select-Object -Property DisplayName, Action, Profile
entries.description: Shows which inbound firewall rules are active and whether they allow or block traffic.
entries.example: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Enabled True | Select-Object -Property DisplayName, Action, Profile

entries.title: Open a port in the firewall
entries.description: Lets other devices connect to a TCP port on this PC. Needs an admin window. Only open ports you need.

entries.title: Delete a firewall rule
entries.description: Deletes firewall rules with that display name. Needs an admin window.

entries.title: List user accounts on this PC
entries.description: Shows local accounts and whether each is enabled.

entries.title: Generate a random secret or password
entries.description: Creates a cryptographically secure random string from the given number of random bytes. Good for passwords and API secrets.

entries.title: Open PowerShell as administrator
entries.description: Opens a new PowerShell window with admin rights after a UAC prompt. Use it for commands that say access denied.

entries.title: Search for an app to install
entries.description: Searches the Windows Package Manager catalog. Note the Id column, which is the most reliable way to install.

entries.title: Install an app with winget
entries.description: Finds and installs an app by name. If several match, winget lists them; then install by Id instead.

entries.title: Install an app by its exact winget Id
entries.description: Installs exactly the package you mean, using the Id shown by winget search, e.g. Git.Git.

entries.title: List apps with updates available
entries.description: Shows installed apps that have a newer version in winget, without installing anything.

entries.title: Update all apps with winget
entries.description: Upgrades every app winget knows how to update. Some installers may show prompts or need closing apps.

entries.title: List installed apps (winget)
entries.description: Shows installed apps, including ones not installed by winget, with their Id and version.

entries.title: Uninstall an app with winget
entries.description: Removes an installed app. Its settings or data may be deleted too.

entries.title: Save a list of installed apps to a file
entries.description: Writes installed apps to a JSON file you can import on another PC with winget import.

entries.title: Install a package with Chocolatey
entries.description: Installs a package from Chocolatey without prompting. Needs an admin window.

entries.title: Update all Chocolatey packages
entries.description: Upgrades every package installed with Chocolatey. Needs an admin window.

entries.title: List Chocolatey packages
entries.description: Lists packages installed with Chocolatey (version 2 and later).

entries.title: Install the Scoop package manager
entries.description: Downloads and runs Scoop's official installer for your user, no admin needed. Requires the RemoteSigned execution policy.

entries.title: Install an app with Scoop
entries.description: Installs an app into your user folder without admin rights.

entries.title: Search for an app in Scoop
entries.description: Searches the Scoop buckets you have added for matching apps.

entries.title: Update all Scoop apps
entries.description: Updates every app installed with Scoop. Run scoop update first to refresh Scoop itself.

entries.title: Install a PowerShell module
entries.description: Installs a module from the PowerShell Gallery for your account only, so no admin is needed.

entries.title: List installed PowerShell modules
entries.description: Shows every PowerShell module installed on this PC and where it lives.

entries.title: Start a new git repository
entries.description: Turns the current folder into a git repository by creating a hidden .git folder.

entries.title: Clone a repository
entries.description: Downloads a copy of a repository, with its full history, into a new folder named after it.

entries.title: Show what has changed (git status)
entries.description: Shows the current branch, staged changes, unstaged changes and untracked files.

entries.title: Stage all changes
entries.description: Stages every new, changed and deleted file for the next commit. Undo with git restore --staged.

entries.title: Stage a specific file
entries.description: Stages one file (or folder) for the next commit.

entries.title: Commit staged changes
entries.description: Saves the staged changes as a new commit with a message describing what changed.

entries.title: Change the last commit message
entries.description: Replaces the last commit's message, and adds any staged changes to it. Avoid on commits you already pushed.

entries.title: Push commits to the remote
entries.description: Uploads your commits on the current branch to its remote branch.

entries.title: Push a new branch and set its upstream
entries.description: Publishes a new local branch to origin and links them, so later git push and git pull need no arguments.

entries.title: Pull the latest changes
entries.description: Downloads new commits from the remote and merges them into your current branch.

entries.title: List branches
entries.description: Lists local and remote branches. The current one is marked with *.

entries.title: Create a new branch and switch to it
entries.description: Creates a branch from where you are and moves onto it. Same as git checkout -b.

entries.title: Switch to another branch
entries.description: Moves to an existing branch. Git refuses if uncommitted changes would be overwritten; commit or stash first.

entries.title: Merge a branch into the current branch
entries.description: Brings another branch's commits into the branch you are on. Conflicts must be fixed and committed.

entries.title: Delete a merged local branch
entries.description: Deletes a local branch, but only if its work is already merged, so nothing is lost.

entries.title: Stash uncommitted changes
entries.description: Puts your uncommitted changes aside so you get a clean working tree. Add -u to include new files. Bring them back with git stash pop.

entries.title: Restore stashed changes
entries.description: Reapplies the most recent stash and removes it from the stash list. Conflicts can happen if files changed since.

entries.title: Show commit history as a graph
entries.description: Shows one line per commit with a branch graph and branch and tag names. Press Q to exit.

entries.title: Show the history of one file
entries.description: Lists every commit that changed a file, with the changes, following it across renames.

entries.title: See who last changed each line of a file
entries.description: Shows the commit, author and date for every line in a file.

entries.title: Show unstaged changes
entries.description: Shows line-by-line changes you have not staged yet.

entries.title: Show staged changes
entries.description: Shows exactly what will go into the next commit.

entries.title: Undo the last commit but keep the changes
entries.description: Removes the last commit and leaves its changes staged, ready to fix and recommit. Avoid on commits already pushed.

entries.title: Unstage a file
entries.description: Takes a file out of the staging area but keeps your edits.

entries.title: Discard changes to a file
entries.description: Throws away uncommitted edits to a file and restores the last committed version. The edits cannot be recovered.

entries.title: Discard all uncommitted changes
entries.description: Resets every tracked file to the last commit, wiping all uncommitted edits. New untracked files stay.

entries.title: Delete untracked files
entries.description: Permanently deletes new files and folders git does not track. Preview first with git clean -nd.

entries.title: Undo a pushed commit with a new commit
entries.description: Creates a new commit that reverses a previous one. Safe for shared branches since history is not rewritten.

entries.title: Show remote repositories
entries.description: Lists the remotes (like origin) and the URLs used to fetch and push.

entries.title: Connect a repository to a remote
entries.description: Links your local repo to a remote, such as a new empty GitHub repo, under the name origin.

entries.title: List tags
entries.description: Lists tags in the repository, often used for release versions.

entries.title: Create a version tag
entries.description: Creates an annotated tag on the current commit, e.g. v1.2.0. Push it with git push origin --tags.

entries.title: Add a pattern to .gitignore
entries.description: Appends a line to .gitignore so git stops showing matching files, e.g. node_modules/ or *.log. Creates the file if missing.

params.name: pattern
params.description: File, folder or pattern to ignore

entries.title: Stop tracking a file but keep it locally
entries.description: Removes a file from git without deleting it from disk. Add it to .gitignore so it is not added again.

entries.title: Set your git name
entries.description: Sets the author name recorded on your commits on this PC.

entries.title: Set your git email
entries.description: Sets the email recorded on your commits. Use the email linked to your GitHub account.

entries.title: Check Node.js and npm versions
entries.description: Prints the installed Node.js and npm versions, which also confirms they are on your PATH.

entries.title: Start a new Node.js project
entries.description: Creates a package.json with default values in the current folder.

entries.title: Install a project's dependencies
entries.description: Installs everything listed in package.json into node_modules, and may update package-lock.json.

entries.title: Add a package to the project
entries.description: Installs a package and adds it to dependencies in package.json.

entries.title: Add a development-only package
entries.description: Installs a package that is only needed while developing, such as a test runner or linter, under devDependencies.

entries.title: Remove a package from the project
entries.description: Removes a package from node_modules and package.json.

entries.title: Run a script from package.json
entries.description: Runs a script defined in the scripts section of package.json, e.g. build, dev or lint.

entries.title: Start the development server
entries.description: Runs the dev script, which in Vite, Next.js and similar projects starts a local server with live reload.

entries.title: Run the project's tests
entries.description: Runs the test script from package.json.

entries.title: List the scripts in package.json
entries.description: Shows every script you can run with npm run, and the command behind each.

entries.title: Install a command-line tool globally
entries.description: Installs a package so its command works in any folder, e.g. typescript for tsc.

entries.title: List outdated packages
entries.description: Shows dependencies that have newer versions available: current, wanted and latest.

entries.title: Update packages within allowed versions
entries.description: Updates dependencies to the newest versions allowed by the ranges in package.json.

entries.title: Run a package's command without installing it
entries.description: Downloads a package temporarily if needed and runs its command. Only run packages you trust.

entries.title: Create a new Vite app (React, Vue...)
entries.description: Scaffolds a new frontend project and asks which framework you want, such as React, Vue or Svelte.

entries.title: Clear the npm cache
entries.description: Deletes npm's download cache. Can fix corrupted-package or checksum errors during installs.

entries.title: Delete node_modules and reinstall
entries.description: Deletes node_modules and installs everything fresh. Fixes many strange build errors; can take a while.

entries.title: Run a JavaScript file with Node
entries.description: Runs a .js file with Node.js.

entries.title: Install dependencies with Yarn
entries.description: Installs dependencies listed in package.json using Yarn and its yarn.lock file.

entries.title: Add a package with Yarn
entries.description: Installs a package and adds it to package.json. Add -D for a dev dependency.

entries.title: Install dependencies with pnpm
entries.description: Installs dependencies with pnpm, which saves disk space by sharing packages between projects.

entries.title: Add a package with pnpm
entries.description: Installs a package and adds it to package.json. Add -D for a dev dependency.

entries.title: Check the Python version
entries.description: Prints the Python version on your PATH. If it opens the Microsoft Store, Python is not really installed.

entries.title: List installed Python versions
entries.description: Uses the Python launcher to show every installed Python version. Run a specific one with py -3.12.

entries.title: Run a Python script
entries.description: Runs a .py file with the Python on your PATH, or the venv's Python if one is active.

entries.title: Create a virtual environment
entries.description: Creates an isolated Python environment in a .venv folder so project packages do not mix with others.

entries.title: Activate the virtual environment
entries.description: Makes python and pip use the project's .venv. If it says running scripts is disabled, allow scripts with Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned first.

entries.title: Leave the virtual environment
entries.description: Turns off the active venv so python points at your system Python again.

entries.title: Install a Python package
entries.description: Installs a package with pip for the current Python or active venv.

entries.title: Install packages from requirements.txt
entries.description: Installs every package listed in the project's requirements.txt.

entries.title: Save installed packages to requirements.txt
entries.command: python -m pip freeze | Out-File -FilePath requirements.txt -Encoding ascii
entries.description: Writes the exact versions of installed packages to requirements.txt, overwriting it.
entries.example: python -m pip freeze | Out-File -FilePath requirements.txt -Encoding ascii

entries.title: List installed Python packages
entries.description: Shows every package installed in the current Python or venv.

entries.title: Upgrade a Python package
entries.description: Installs the newest version of a package.

entries.title: Upgrade pip itself
entries.description: Updates pip to the latest version, which fixes many install errors.

entries.title: Uninstall a Python package
entries.description: Removes a package from the current Python or venv without asking for confirmation.

entries.title: Serve the current folder over HTTP
entries.description: Starts a simple web server for the current folder at http://localhost:PORT. Press Ctrl+C to stop. Not for production use.

entries.title: Run Python tests with pytest
entries.description: Finds and runs tests in files named test_*.py. Install pytest first.

entries.title: Create a virtual environment with uv
entries.description: Creates a .venv very quickly using uv, a fast Python package manager.

entries.title: List running containers
entries.description: Shows running containers with their ID, image, ports and name.

entries.title: List all containers, including stopped
entries.description: Shows every container, including ones that have exited.

entries.title: List Docker images
entries.description: Shows images downloaded or built on this machine, with their sizes.

entries.title: Run a container interactively
entries.description: Starts a container connected to your terminal and removes it when you exit.

entries.title: Run a container in the background with a port
entries.description: Starts a container in the background and maps a port, written host:container, e.g. 8080:80.

entries.title: Open a shell inside a running container
entries.description: Opens a shell inside a container so you can look around. Use bash instead of sh if the image has it.

entries.title: Follow a container's logs
entries.description: Shows a container's output and keeps streaming new lines. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

entries.title: Stop a container
entries.description: Gracefully stops a running container. Start it again with docker start.

entries.title: Remove a container
entries.description: Deletes a stopped container and any data stored inside it that is not in a volume.

entries.title: Build an image from a Dockerfile
entries.description: Builds an image from the Dockerfile in the current folder and names it.

params.name: tag
params.description: Image name and tag, e.g. myapp:1.0

entries.title: Start services with Docker Compose
entries.description: Starts every service in docker-compose.yml in the background, building or pulling images if needed.

entries.title: Stop and remove Compose services
entries.description: Stops and removes the containers and networks from docker-compose.yml. Volumes are kept unless you add -v.

entries.title: Show container CPU and memory usage
entries.description: Shows a snapshot of each container's CPU, memory and network use.

entries.title: Show Docker disk usage
entries.description: Shows how much space images, containers, volumes and build cache use.

entries.title: Remove all unused Docker data
entries.description: Deletes stopped containers, unused networks, unused images and build cache to free space. Asks first.

entries.title: List installed .NET SDKs
entries.description: Shows every .NET SDK version installed and where it lives.

entries.title: Create a new .NET console app
entries.description: Creates a C# console project in a new folder.

entries.title: Build a .NET project
entries.description: Compiles the project or solution in the current folder.

entries.title: Run a .NET project
entries.description: Builds and runs the project in the current folder.

entries.title: Run .NET tests
entries.description: Builds and runs tests in the solution or test project in the current folder.

entries.title: Add a NuGet package
entries.description: Adds a NuGet package reference to the project in the current folder.

entries.title: Check Rust and Cargo versions
entries.description: Prints the installed Rust compiler and Cargo versions.

entries.title: Create a new Rust project
entries.description: Creates a new Rust binary project in a folder with Cargo.toml and src\main.rs, and starts a git repo.

entries.title: Build a Rust project
entries.description: Compiles the project in debug mode into the target folder.

entries.title: Run a Rust project
entries.description: Builds and runs the project in the current folder.

entries.title: Run Rust tests
entries.description: Builds and runs all tests in the project.

entries.title: Add a Rust dependency
entries.description: Adds a crate to Cargo.toml at its latest version.

entries.title: Check the Go version
entries.description: Prints the installed Go version.

entries.title: Start a new Go module
entries.description: Creates go.mod in the current folder. The module path is usually like github.com/you/project.

entries.title: Run a Go program
entries.description: Compiles and runs the main package in the current folder.

entries.title: Build a Go program
entries.description: Compiles the package in the current folder into an .exe.

entries.title: Run all Go tests
entries.description: Runs tests in the current module and all its subfolders.

entries.title: Add a Go dependency
entries.description: Adds or updates a dependency in go.mod.

entries.title: Check the Java version
entries.description: Prints the installed Java runtime version.

entries.title: Compile a Java file
entries.description: Compiles a .java file into a .class file in the same folder.

entries.title: Run a single Java file directly
entries.description: Compiles and runs a single .java file in one step (Java 11 and later).

entries.title: Run a .jar file
entries.description: Runs a Java application packaged as a .jar file.

entries.title: Build a Maven project
entries.description: Cleans, compiles, tests and packages the Maven project in the current folder into target\.

entries.title: Connect to a server over SSH
entries.description: Opens a remote shell on another machine. Write the destination as user@host.

entries.title: Connect over SSH with a key file
entries.description: Connects using a specific private key, such as a .pem file from a cloud provider.

entries.title: Create a new SSH key
entries.description: Creates a key pair in your .ssh folder. Press Enter to accept the default file, and it asks before overwriting an existing key.

params.name: email
params.description: Label for the key, usually your email

entries.title: Copy my SSH public key to the clipboard
entries.description: Copies your public key so you can paste it into GitHub, GitLab or a server. Never share the file without .pub.

entries.title: Install my public key on a server (ssh-copy-id)
entries.description: Adds your public key to a Linux server so you can log in without a password. Asks for the password one last time.

entries.title: Test SSH access to GitHub
entries.description: Checks your SSH key works with GitHub. A greeting with your username means success.

entries.title: Forget a server's old host key
entries.description: Removes a host from known_hosts. Fixes REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED after a server is rebuilt.

entries.title: Copy a file to or from a server (scp)
entries.description: Copies a file over SSH. Write the remote side as user@host:path.

entries.title: Sort the lines of a file
entries.description: Prints a file's lines in alphabetical order. Add -Descending to reverse it.

entries.title: Remove duplicate lines
entries.description: Prints each distinct line once, sorted. Comparison ignores upper and lower case.

entries.title: Count how often each line appears
entries.command: Get-Content -Path <file> | Group-Object | Sort-Object -Property Count -Descending | Select-Object -Property Count, Name
entries.description: Groups identical lines and shows how many times each appears, most common first.
entries.example: Get-Content -Path .\ips.txt | Group-Object | Sort-Object -Property Count -Descending | Select-Object -Property Count, Name

entries.title: Count lines, words and characters
entries.description: Counts the lines, words and characters in a text file.

entries.title: Pretty-print a JSON file
entries.description: Reads JSON and prints it indented so it is easier to read.

entries.title: Read a value from a JSON file
entries.description: Prints one top-level field from a JSON file, e.g. the version in package.json.

entries.title: Convert a CSV file to JSON
entries.description: Turns each CSV row into a JSON object and saves the array to a file.

entries.title: View a CSV file as a table
entries.description: Shows a CSV file in neat columns in the terminal.

entries.title: Open a CSV in a sortable, filterable window
entries.description: Opens the CSV in a window where you can sort columns and filter rows by typing.

entries.title: Filter CSV rows by a column value
entries.description: Shows only rows where a column equals a value. Matching ignores upper and lower case.

entries.title: Count CSV rows by a column
entries.command: Import-Csv -Path <file> | Group-Object -Property <column> | Sort-Object -Property Count -Descending | Select-Object -Property Count, Name
entries.description: Shows how many rows have each value in a column, most common first, like a pivot table count.
entries.example: Import-Csv -Path .\orders.csv | Group-Object -Property Status | Sort-Object -Property Count -Descending | Select-Object -Property Count, Name

entries.title: Save the process list to a CSV file
entries.command: Get-Process | Select-Object -Property Name, Id, CPU, WorkingSet64 | Export-Csv -Path <file> -NoTypeInformation
entries.description: An example of saving any command's output as CSV for Excel: pick properties with Select-Object, then Export-Csv.
entries.example: Get-Process | Select-Object -Property Name, Id, CPU, WorkingSet64 | Export-Csv -Path .\processes.csv -NoTypeInformation

entries.title: Copy a file's contents to the clipboard
entries.description: Puts the text of a file on the clipboard, ready to paste.

entries.title: Show what is on the clipboard
entries.description: Prints the clipboard's text, which you can pipe into other commands.

entries.title: Base64-encode text
entries.description: Converts text to Base64 using UTF-8.

entries.title: Decode Base64 text
entries.description: Turns Base64 back into readable UTF-8 text.

entries.title: Get the SHA-256 hash of some text
entries.description: Hashes a string rather than a file, encoded as UTF-8 with no trailing newline.

entries.title: Generate a GUID / UUID
entries.description: Creates a new random globally unique identifier.

entries.title: Show help and examples for a command
entries.description: Shows usage examples for a cmdlet. If help is missing, run Update-Help in an admin window first.

entries.title: Open a command's documentation online
entries.description: Opens the official Microsoft documentation page for a cmdlet in your browser.

entries.title: Download the latest help files
entries.description: Downloads full help for installed modules. Windows PowerShell needs an admin window for this.

entries.title: Show a command's syntax
entries.description: Prints the parameter sets a command accepts, in one compact block.

entries.title: Find commands by name
entries.description: Lists commands, functions and programs matching a wildcard, e.g. *firewall* or *-Service.

entries.title: Find where a command comes from (which)
entries.description: Shows whether a name is a cmdlet, alias, function or program, and for programs the full path of the .exe.
entries.example: Get-Command -Name python | Select-Object -Property Name, CommandType, Source

entries.title: Find every copy of a program on PATH
entries.description: Lists all matching programs on PATH in search order. The first one wins, which explains wrong-version problems.

entries.title: See what an alias stands for
entries.description: Shows which command an alias such as ls, cat or gci runs.

entries.title: Show the PowerShell version
entries.description: Shows the PowerShell version and edition. Windows PowerShell is 5.1; PowerShell 7 is the newer cross-platform one.

entries.title: Clear the screen
entries.description: Clears the terminal. Same as cls or clear.

entries.title: Show command history for this session
entries.description: Lists the commands you ran in this window with their ID numbers.

entries.title: Search past commands
entries.description: Finds old commands containing some text across all sessions. Ctrl+R searches interactively too.

entries.title: Re-run a command from history
entries.description: Runs a previous command again by its ID from Get-History.

entries.title: List all aliases
entries.description: Shows every alias, such as ls for Get-ChildItem and cat for Get-Content.

entries.title: Create a command alias
entries.description: Makes a short name for a command in this session. Put the line in your $PROFILE to keep it. Aliases cannot include arguments.

entries.title: Edit your PowerShell profile
entries.description: Opens your startup script in Notepad, creating it first if needed. Aliases and functions there load in every new window.

entries.title: Reload your PowerShell profile
entries.description: Runs your profile again so edits take effect without opening a new window.

entries.title: Time how long a command takes
entries.description: Runs a command and reports how long it took. The command's own output is hidden.

entries.title: Show how long the last command took
entries.description: Shows the runtime of the command you just ran, without having to run it again.

entries.title: Record everything in this session to a file
entries.description: Saves all commands and output in this window to a text file until you run Stop-Transcript.

entries.title: Show the exit code of the last program
entries.description: Prints the exit code of the last program you ran. 0 usually means success.

entries.title: Show full details of the last error
entries.description: Shows the full message, stack trace and location of the most recent error. Get-Error is not in Windows PowerShell.

entries.title: Run a PowerShell script
entries.description: Runs a .ps1 script file. If it is blocked, check the execution policy entries.

entries.title: Run a Command Prompt (cmd) command
entries.description: Runs a classic cmd.exe command or .bat file from PowerShell, for things like mklink or dir /s.

entries.title: Fix garbled characters in output (UTF-8)
entries.description: Makes this window read program output as UTF-8, fixing garbled accents, symbols and emoji from tools like git or node.
